newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran quake kills at least 100, injures 250.
newsitem.headline: Iran quake kills at least 100, injures 250.

text.p: A strong earthquake killed at least 100 people and injured 250 in northwestern Iran on Friday, Iranian state television said.
The earthquake, measuring 5.5 on Richter scale, hit the city of Ardabil and the town of Meshkinshahr in an area near Iran's border with Azerbaijan at 4.27 p.m. (1257 GMT), the television said.

"The country's Natural Disaster Headquarters announced, with regret, that at least 100 of our compatriots have lost their lives and over 250 people were injured," said the television, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.
The quake lasted 30 seconds and also caused considerable damage in many of the surrounding districts in Ardabil province which borders Azerbaijan, it said.
Rescue teams rushed to the stricken areas to help the survivors, the television said.
Ardabil is an agricultural province inhabited mainly by Iran's Azeri minority. It is one of Iran's coldests regions with regularly freezing temperatures during the winter.
The tremor hit the Ardabil area some 16 hours after a strong earthquake killed nearly 50 people in and around the town of Quetta in Pakistan's Baluchistan province across Iran's southeastern border.
A Pakistani government seismic centre in the northwestern town of Peshawar measured that earthquake at 6.2 on the Richter scale.

The Iranian news agency IRNA earlier said a quake also measuring 5.5 on the Richter scale hit the western Iranian city of Sanandaj at about the same time as the tremor hit Ardabil, some 350 km (220 miles) away.
There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage in Sanandaj, a Kurdish-populated provincial capital, it said.
Iran's northern province of Gilan on the Caspian Sea coast was also shaken by a tremor measuring about four on the Richter scale, but there was no damage, IRNA added.
Force four and five tremors are powerful enough to cause heavy damage in in populated areas.
In early February, two earthquakes measuring 6.1 and 5.4 on the Richter scale killed at least 79 people and injured 260 in a mountainous region in northeastern Iran.
Earthquakes hit Iran regularly. The worst recorded one, measuring 7.3 on the Richter scale, killed 35,000 people in Gilan and neighbouring Zanjan province in 1990.
